review:
cortina has such a beautiful energy. as a therapist, she's encouraging and supportive while e helping to push you towards change. she has the gift of blending spiritual wisdom with counseling  knowledge that really leads to healing. i love how she uses adversity to move her forward in her own life and is able to help clients do the same.

the office is in a great location in the heart of winter park and has a dedicated parking lot. she sees clients through an appointment only basis. i know she also offers discounted rates for package purchases of sessions but otherwise has a pretty standard self-pay rate. i believe she does telehealth and of course in person sessions. she has an online portal too so clients can do scheduling and  paperwork all online (but has paper copies if the old school approach is more comfy). 

ps! she has a book! so if you're interested in checking her out before you schedule it might be worth it to grab a copy and hear from her through her writing.

recently had cosmetic surgery. i was only looking to get a (bbl) brazilian butt lift with fat transfer.  i'm a very petite woman already (108lbs) just never had a butt. dr. mowlavi talked me into doing all this other stuff like a mini tummy tuck for loose skin,  i didn't have a lot of loose skin and  have pictures to prove it.  he said it would be the size of a c-section scar 4-6 inches.  i woke up to an incision from hip to hip.  his office said recovery is quicker with his vaser lipo and renuvion techniques. this is by far the worst pain and recovery ever. i would never recommend this for anyone! they didn't have much to do with me after they got my money ($25k not including stay and airfare and 3days extra for a nurse because i couldn't get in and out of bed. for total of 30k)
i went in everyday for first week for massages.  dr. mowlavi only saw me the day after surgery for 2 mins to look at his work.  i tried to set up a post op a week after because i was very unhappy with results.  he knew of my disappointment because my massage therapist told him.  he didn't come to the office for our appointment time.  so i rescheduled for the next day at 3pm for video chat.  again 3pm came and no dr.  we called his office several times and they said he was with other consultations and would call me. we waited until 5:30pm dr never called in, and then the office was closed.  i was beyond furious this is 2 appt he's missed and not a single call from anyone in the office to reschedule or anything.  so i called claudia and she acted like he'd get back to me and she'd be in it first thing.  she's a huge liar,  she's never had this surgery done and tells all the new clients how you could hop on a plane in a week no problem.  so instead the next day i got an email from their assistant mimi with my before and after video and said if i had any questions to email them. that was last week on feb 4th. i have yet to have a post op appt or even a scheduled appt with dr.  he doesn't care and has completely disregarded me as a patient. now i'm still in tons of pain,  my swelling will not subside and i have to go to drs to have my stomach drained of the fluid because it's moving like a waterbed which is called a seroma. it's been a nightmare.  his office has done nothing but lie and avoid me. i was told he does this with all his patients.  i'm still laid up in bed and i have children and a job i can't do.  
here is a pic of my supposed small c-section scar i have to live with. 
 pay attention and do not sign the arbitration agreement clause.  you legally don't have too!
notice that dr. mowlavi never post before and healed after results.

review:
i came to innovative express care because my primary was moving here. i feel like it is very important to write honest reviews, especially when it comes to your health. i have been unfortunate enough to experience some not so great healthcare, and it has made me very much appreciate how attentive and caring innovative express care is. i see jenna benoit, pa-c, for primary care and have been seeing her for many years. i am really happy that jenna decided to move here because it feels like it runs on an integrated care model. they are expanding to offer wellness through ketamine infusion, cbd oil, among others. they also have an innovative med spa which i also think is great. the way they've branched out is impressed and i enjoy that they keep the same type of model. their patient portal is very easy to use and tracks your health in one setting. i am able to easily send messages and ask about prescriptions. they also have telemedicine which is helpful for when i don't need to come in/am busy. they have social workers here, too, so you can receive therapy. again, definitely feels like an integrated healthcare model being used. 

aside from going here for my primary care, i have gone to their urgent care on several occasions. my primary is kind, caring, and patient with me; she knows me well but doesn't get annoyed when i reach out, make requests, or send her many messages. as a person with anxiety, this is special to met because it helps me feel at ease. i've had the opportunity to receive care from jayme, michelle, and lindsay (all pas) in the past when i had to come in for urgent care and they were all really wonderful and kind. kindness goes a long way and it extends to their nurses who've always said hi to me and made me feel welcomed and comfortable. there was a period of time where i had to come in a few times a week or once a week and everyone from the nurses to the receptionists have always been welcoming. i definitely appreciate innovative express care and their staff; i encourage everyone to come here! be mindful that if you're coming for urgent care, you're definitely going to have to wait. it's just how it is, but i've never waited for urgent care more than 15-20 minutes; make an appointment online ahead of time is the best suggestion!

i went to see someone here for an annual check-up. i had called my insurance before to confirm it would be compensated as part of my plan. they confirmed it. zoom billed it inaccurately, and i've had to pay out of pocket. i was told i would receive a refund which i have not seen. they then ignored my several emails to adjust it. i then wasted half a dozen calls with their useless billing department, nichole, who didn't adjust anything. do not come here unless you want to be billed inaccurately and have to follow-up needlessly. go anywhere else.

two hour wait and then they offered a virtual doctor on zoom at the end.  for that, just let me take it from home and zoom right???  it better cost less.   and i can just chill from the house.   i've been waiting 2 hours and still have not been seen.  same with another lady in here and she blew up.  they tried to charge for her waiting 2 hours and wanting to reschedule.  she never even talked to a doctor!!!!    i asked how many doctors on staff - only one.   and they were busy taking patients and appointments.  wtf.  

all business poor customer patient sat.   i'm out man.

i set up an appointment online for a skin reaction. when i got to the office i was surprised 1) that i would be attended to by a nurse practitioner rather than a doctor 2) that the visit would be performed via video conference.

i would never have gone in for a skin reaction had the provider been transparent that the visit were be to performed via video conference.

in short, the combination of the video conference and poor bedside manner from the nurse practitioner led to misdiagnoses for which i had to follow up with another care provider for secondary issues caused by the misdiagnoses.

i pursued review of my case, and the customer experience was abysmal. weeks for email responses, promises for phone calls, and unable to provide any documentation of the investigation that was said to have happened internally, or, at the very least, an apology. i would highly advise against this care provider and intend to pursue legal action against them.

wish i had read these reviews before going there..
my eyes were itching and i presumed i was having a skin reaction so i went here two weeks ago before a business meeting..
they were incredibly slow and could not get their internet to take my insurance card..
finally they set up a zoom meeting with the 'doctor' and turns out it was a pa who looked and acted like she was 12..
i repeatedly tried to explain that it was the skin under my eyes that was itching but they still insisted on making me take a worthless eye exam..
i left with a prescription for ocular antihistamine drops and antibiotics that did absolutely nothing to help me..
i finally went next door and purchased otc topical anti-itch medication and bacitracin which at least helped a little but decided i would never be going back..
the kicker is that i just received a bill for $179 which was charged to my credit card.. dont even think of going here if you are sick!

just had another great visit at zoom care. from the front desk staff to the awesome doctor amy theppote, dpm, it was another seamless visit. although we certainly don't want to have to visit, when we are in need of care, especially quick, convenient, this is our place to go. dr amy was wonderful with our son who broke his toe. we really appreciated her kindness and knowledge. she is fantastic!  so awesome to have a doctor of podiatry at zoom care!

very blessed by the care and attention i have received at caduceus. afraid that i may be contagious with the flu, the virtual visit with the urgent care confirmed my fears and they called in the medication i needed.  cannot stress this enough, this years's flu is extremely painful and getting the medication needed asap is important. so thankful to shital patel np & tanya lizarde mvp for the compassionate care!

my doctor was dr. kulak. we had a great experience because of him. he answered all questions and provided information clearly, whether in office, email or through video conference. even after we got pregnant and switched to a regular ob gyn he was willing to support me. the staff at genesis were kind and friendly which you need for those 630 am blood withdrawal

i got the radiant iv drip. i wanted vitamin c for health reasons and they recommended the radiant drip. it has a lower level of vitamin c than if you get the vitamin c by itself. i also tacked on vitamin d for an addition $29. totally worth it. they have specials as well and will let you know what is available. staff is informative and friendly. they check your vitals, and you also get to video chat with a nurse to check your medical condition as well as answer any questions you may have. i want to do the hyperbaric chamber next. my skin felt hydrated and soft as an additional bonus to the iv drip. wasn't there for that, but who is complaining. not this woman.

i received a phone call the beginning of december from this company with the name of the person that would be handling my cpap machine order.  preferred received the prescription and order from sleep telemedicine services, who performed the two sleep studies on me.  ten days later i called and was finally connected to the cpap machine contact.  she informed me she hadn't even looked at the order.  while i was on the phone with her, she looked at the order and then stated she wasn't even going to submit it to my insurance because she didn't feel it would be approved.  she also felt after looking at the prescription that i didn't even need a cpap machine.  she went on and on about how doctors write prescriptions that aren't necessary, and she wasn't going to waste her time.  she ended the call stating she would reach out to my doctor and let them know.  

the next day i called sleep telemedicine services and they submitted the order to aa medical.  it was approved by my insurance the next day.  two days later i received my machine and wonderful training by the therapist at aa medical.  

never ever will i use preferred for any dme!!

absolutely the easiest doctor visit ever.  done from the comfort of my own home.  on top of that the doctor was on time and was so nice!  i used to use this video conference dr visits all the time in the mainland but this service was even better than i could have ever imagined!  thanks dr anegawa for the outstanding care!

cedar count is the highest since the early 1900's and i couldn't shake the sinus pressure and lost nasal drip. so i reached out to plush care thru my insurance and was able to get an appointment within 2 hours. meet the doctor online video chat and told him what was going on he asked a few questions. he wrote a prescription i picked it up the same days and now two days later i am 95% back to normal just a small infrequent cough which will probably be gone by tomorrow. so easy and convenient.

i tried plushcare this week, and i was quite impressed. i have a telemedicine service that is free through my insurance, but i often feel like the medical doctors are hesitant to prescribe medication unless you are in really bad shape. plushcare had a $15 copay for me with my insurance, plus 30-day trial membership, then $9.99/month. so this time, i had the flu for a week and developed bronchitis, i couldn't sleep through the night due to my hacking cough. dr. klenk was so upbeat and compassionate; she got me hooked up with needed meds for my bronchitis, and also sent a refill of one of my maintenance meds. this was on new year's eve afternoon...by dinnertime, i had already picked up my prescriptions from the pharmacy and was on the road to healing. i will definitely turn to them again.

zoomcare is the worst ever.  1st of all, you won't see a doctor, you will sure a pa (physicians assistant).  the pas we saw at bridgeport didn't look like they were out of high school and one had just started at zoom.  my wife went in on january 1st only because we were the only ones open.  the pa then prescribed a weeks worth of docecylcine (sp?) and a at the end of the week she was 75% better, but not completely well.  i had the same condition and my ent prescribed 22 days of docecycline (sp?) and i am 100% better.  on january 20th, my wife goes into zoom and asks a different pa, "hey, i am not 100% better.  could you prescribe another 7 days of the antibiotic".  this is where analysis paralysis sets in to the apparent high school age pa.  he doesn't know what to do, so he sends my wife to the hospital to get an x-ray (zoom bridgeport has no imaging capabilities).  we get the x-ray and zoom promises to get back to us by 6 pm.  no response.  i call back on jan 20 and the call center woman says she has no info for us.  at that time, my wife gives the call center woman her authorization to speak with me about this issue (hippa) but as i find out later, zoom never makes a note of my wife's verbal authorization.  i call back the morning of jan 21st and zoom won't tell me anything.  i then ask the probable high school girl age girl who answers the phone at the call center to simply send my wife an email to update us as to next steps, i.e. docecycline prescription.  the young girl at the call center says isn't sure if she can send my wife an email to provide an update on the pa's decision to extend a prescription for the antibiotics or feedback on the x-ray.  

if you go to zoom, be prepared for "young and dumb" excuses, care provided by pas and not physicians and no one at this office will answer your call, rather it goes to a non-healthcare operator who will continue the snowball of incompetency.  they aren't on epic or similar ehr.

bottom line is you must be ready to be seen by non-doctors, with no imaging back up at this center and you must be ready to endure broken promises and incompetent follow up.

they won't tell you up front how much any of their services are, so you have no idea how much they will bill you for. and, since you have to sign an agreement to pay beforehand, there's no recourse. 
also, the doctors consult via video chat. the one person who works there acts as their hands. 
i decided to wait to see my regular doctor instead.

i am hooked on lifeplus pharmacy!!!!!
family owned, caring, compassionate and knowledgeable staff. i am thankful that i found lifeplus pharmacy, my meds are always on time. i had telemedicine with dr. singh once, a very caring, knowledgeable and compassionate md. what a great experience. ritue, a wonderful pharmacist takes care of her clients and makes sure that everyone gets treated respectfully and compassionately. last night i had my vitamin and hydration iv treatments.... wow  it only took few minutes after to feel rejuvenated and ready for the new year. i highly recommend lifeplus pharmacy.

first of all, i'd like to say that i don't think i can't even put into words how blessed i feel for having met dr. pawel stachowicz on 9-5-19  i originally met dr. pawel for a free consultation.(i was skeptical) but it was free!
i figured what did i have to lose? most plastic surgeons charge for a consultation.
the date of my consultation i miss judged how long it would take me to get to his office and was very late. i was stressed and had anxiety because i thought i would miss my appointment which is hard enough for me to make.
i text dr. pawel to let him know i would be late. he said "no problem let me know when you have arrived"
when i finally reached the office dr. pawel greeted me and spent a lot of time with me going over the whole procedure, asking me questions and getting to know me plus doing the exam
i am 53 years old and i wanted a mommy makeover! a much needed breast reduction/lift, lipo and tummy tuck.
i was very specific and telling dr. pawel what i wanted.
that day in his office i was so impressed with dr. pawel and became comfortable with him and his demeanor that by the end of the consultation i listen to my gut feeling and when ahead and schedule the surgery.
normally i would have to do a lot of research and thinking before making such a big decision.
dr. paul  let me pick a day and then later called to confirm and text me everything that we went over. it's nice to have everything in writing so you can refer back to it plus it can all be a little overwhelming trying to remember what your doctor is telling you all at once.
i did call dr. powell a couple more times with questions i forgot to ask during our conversations and he was always available to answer my questions. he usually returned my calls within two hours if i left a message or text.

i had my surgery done at abbott northwestern hospital. that definitely gave me comfort in knowing i had a full anesthesia department by my side, not to mention it was much less expensive than a surgery center. i believe that's why dr. pawel is able to keep his prices so low, usually the surgery is about the same as the surgery centers fees in my experience.
the nurses that assisted dr. pawel  were great! i have to give a shout out to them as well as the anesthesiologist.
dr. pawel did such an amazing job! my boobs look better than when i was 20 years old! the body contouring and tummy tuck makes me look and feel like a teenager again. dr. pawel is an artist! i am very impressed with dr. pawel he is very good at what he does, before during and after my surgery dr. pawel was there. whether it be by phone text or video chat. evenings or weekend appointments! he was able to answer questions when i was out of town about wound care by sending in photos or video chatting. i recommend to anybody who is considering a plastic surgery procedure-especially breast or a tummy tuck- lipo to contact dr. pawel and set up an appointment.  its free!
what have you got to lose other than pounds! :)

i went through a long weekend with a bad ear infection.  i called telehealth on monday morning, president's day, and i was directed to the sanford office.  i went online, read some reviews, and made my appointment for 11 am.  i arrived early because i was in pain, and i knew i needed to fill out paperwork.  when i walked in, the staff was very friendly and i filled out the new patient paperwork while i waited.  i was on the phone with my worried girlfriend, about an ear infection, and it seemed that i was called in minutes by the nurse who guided me through triage and then to the waiting room.  i waited a few minutes and a pa showed up, very nice, asked some more questions, noticed i had a visible outside ear infection, and proceeded with the exam.  i think it took longer for my prescription to be written because i was anxious at that point.  i never expect to walk in and out of a doctor's office in less than a hour, but i did.  i spent over 90 minutes to have my prescription filled, which is for another review.  i was quite please with adventhealth, and during this time, the lobby had around 5 people waiting to be seen.  they did call the people with reservations.

my 1st appointment with dr. wexler was in 2017. i was curious & somewhat apprehensive, as it was to take place over the phone, using telemedicine. 
i should preface my review by saying that the search for a psychiatrist who not only has excellent credentials but with whom you can feel comfortable is not easily accomplished. within minutes of speaking with him i wanted to yell "eureka "! dr. wexler has been working 
with me to manage & "fine tune " my medications. he has also been educating me about depression, anxiety & the "how" & "why" various medications work together -
all helping me emerge from the bleak, black wasteland that i have inhabited for far too long. within the 1st 7 
months of becoming his patient, dr. wexler did more to alleviate my symptoms stemming from major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety & fnd ( functional neurologic disorder) than had been the case for well over 8 yrs. he keeps abreast of the newest developments & advancements in his fields. the passion he has for his specialties is obvious. his written feedback following ea. appt. is prompt as is his response to e-mails. his reports are sent to my other treating physicians & therapist. the result: a team of professionals all working together for the same goal. my confidence in dr. wexler & in his ability to finally let me thrive cannot be overstated. how fortunate i feel to have become his patient!
ea california

my only concern is that i was only with the doctor for about 10 minutes max and she confirmed my ear infection but she also found out that i had a sinus infection and swollen nose... which apparently all connect together. she gave me some antibiotics, a nasal spray, and some probiotics and that was $71 out of pocket... not sure how much they charged my insurance but i was caught off guard because it's definitely a lot higher than expected! my insurance usually covers 100% with a $35 co-pay so i was confused with their charges... they don't give you a receipt on the spot, you have to check the statements online and they make you view your status online.

needed to get my teeth whitened before the wedding. i didn't think i really needed it but the wife to be insisted.  i didn't think the zoom products actually work but went ahead with it.  after an hour, it's safe to say my teeth have never been whiter and brighter.  no more yellow teeth!  i've been getting a lot of compliments on how white and shiny my teeth are.  i guess i really did need it!  the nurse was great and explained each step along the way.  at the end, the owner also gave me some special toothpaste for sensitivity teeth, which i thought was very nice.  fyi the sensitivity wasn't as bad as i had expected it to be.  highly recommend!

first time member at kaiser 1/1/2020. have gotten sick  3 times in the last month. decide to try to seek help and get a prescription through my new health care provider. go through the evisit option only to be advised that i actually need to call the nurse hotline. i do. have to wait 1.5 hours for a call back where in the nurse advises i gargle with saltwater. i do. symptoms worsen by the next day. attempt virtual visit...don't qualify since i haven't had an in person visit yet.  call to make an in person office visit...no availability until tomorrow afternoon and that appts with a diff dr. kaiser permanente...so far u 100% suck and i 100% regret switching over to u. two thumbs down. i'll now be waiting in urgent care for the next 3 hours. god help  me if they tell me to gargle salt water again.

had a virtual appointment with my 18 month old and they needed to do some testing so were going to send someone to our home within 20 minutes! there was some confusion and miscommunication about pricing but they remedied (pun intended) it with excellent customer service.

we will definitely use remedy for our future sick care needs. just a tip- make sure to call and specifically mention your child's age if you're doing a virtual visit.

remedy is a life saver for this mom of 4.

such a good experience with these people. our family has used them twice now. once was strictly a video conference and the second time they did a video and came out to the home to do labwork. overall, both times the care was exceptional and everyone we have dealt with their has had such a caring personality. highly recommended.

i came in because of a sinus infection and they treated me like a human and not a piece of cattle like all of the other doctor's offices i've been to. they diagnosed me, gave me the meds that i needed and i was out the door in  20 minutes. we really like zoom+care. we have also ya amen my daughere to a different location on alberta in portland. the doctor was also very helpful with my daughter and diagnosed her skin rash was  poison ivy or oak. they actually care about their patients and not just shove as many meds as possible into them. we will only use  zoom from now on.

how many stars do you give to a clinic that almost killed you? since zero stars isn't possible i guess i'll have to settle for one star. let this serve as a psa to get your own doctor and to never visit a zoomcare if you value your life. there is a reason you never have to wait at a zoomcare, they want you in and out and fast as physically possible. my obvious symptoms were ignored and i was shoved out the door.

less than 4 hours later after i left zoomcare, where my symptoms were ignored i was experiencing a medical emergency which was only amplified because zoomcare, and their terrible pa ignored my symptoms. if i would have listened to the advice of this zoomcare, and the "super"clinic they referred me to, i would be dead. my husband without a partner and my children without a mother.

so to zoomcare if you're reading this, these are the telltale signs of epiglottitis:
severe sore throat
fever
a muffled or hoarse voice
abnormal, high-pitched sound when breathing in (stridor)
difficulty breathing
difficulty swallowing
drooling

i experienced 6/7 of these symptoms when i came into the clinic, which i told the pa. this pa faked a strep test and sent me on my way after explaining i was having a hard time breathing, in addition to 6 of these 7 tell tale signs of epiglottitis. if you want to see where i ended up at the end of the night, check out my review of the super clinic on ne grand.

there's a reason his location is poorly rated. linsey zocco is a terrible pa. do not see her. i repeat do not see her. i had lunch with a friend today and our conversation went like this:

friend: ugh i had a terrible zoom care experience.
me: which location?
friend: missippi
me: (gasps) no, who did you see?
friend: zocco
me: omg me too!

this is a person that should be in a lab. she should not be dealing with the public. she has a terrible attitude. she doesn't listen to you when you describe what you are experiencing, she says she performs tests that she does not. she is rude, off-putting and gives zoomcare a very bad name. she is the reason i have banned zoomcare for myself and my entire family.

suddenly came down with a stomach flu bug.  called regenerate me and amazing customer service from the get go. the call was disconnected on my end and the reached back out to me to verify i still wanted services. they scheduled me for about 2 hours later and had me do a video chat with a doctor to go over my medical history. 

my nurse, amber, showed up on time. very communicative and informative of everything she was doing, as she was doing it. answered all of my questions and got my iv started.  she stayed right next to me and making sure i was comfortable the entire time and even covered me with my own blanket. 

thank you for this service and we will definitely recommend and use their services again if needed!

this place is horrible.  the last 2 office visits were supposed to be well visits which my insurance pays 100%.  they didn't do that and now are billing for my copayment.  also, when you call they don't return your call.  you get switched from 1 person to the next and then put on hold and then disconnected.  the medical assistant is never available.  i have been trying to get a refill on a prescription for over a week. my pharmacy has called them with no luck either and sent 3 faxes.  i have made close to 24 phone calls.  most of my calls are disconnected.  they switch you all over the place and some tell me that a request has been sent but no one is responding. i left numerous messages with the medical assistants and have not heard anything.  i am out of my medication and now think i will do better with a virtual doctor.  done with this mad house that you wait 2 plus hours to get past your appointment time.

how many stars do you give to a clinic that almost killed you? since zero stars inset possible i guess i'll have to settle for one star. let this serve as a psa to get your own doctor and to never visit a zoomcare if you value your life. there is a reason you never have to wait at a zoomcare, they want you in and out and fast as physically possible. my obvious symptoms were ignored and i was shoved out the door.

after visiting the zoomcare location on mississippi (also a 1 star review) it was recommended that i check out a super clinic for an x-ray. i was at this location 15 minutes after i left the first location.

i explained all over again what i had explained at the previous clinic and they ordered an x-ray. it took a good 45 minutes to get the x-ray, once it was complete i started shaking uncontrollably(later i realized this was probably a spike in my temp). the x-ray guy(he was the only good thing about this clinic) loaded me up with blankets and directed me back to the exam room. i waited another good 45 minutes and suddenly it became very hard to breathe, like my throat was closing off more. i was struggling to breathe and because of this is started to panic and my hands went numb. i called out for the nurse and explained i was having a panic because it was getting more difficult to breathe.

i was injected full of ativan because they thought i was having a panic attack. i was having a panic attack because i couldn't breathe. i wasn't having a random panic attack. they gave me a thick gi drink and told me to drink it. i tried. i couldn't. i explained i could not physically swallow it. the drink kept coming up. they said they didn't see anything on the xray. i was told to "take an uber home and rest. maybe see a gi specialist within 48 hours". 

i thought this was a joke. but i took than damn uber home and was left without a car. i went home, tried to draw a bath and "relax". i started vomiting and it wouldn't stop, but i kept choking as it was happening. i was worried i would asphyxiate. thank god my mother in law was there to take care of my kids because i called the neighbor and she took me to the er at ohsu. my neighbor had become a nurse mere weeks before and she knew i was in respiratory distress within seconds of seeing me. seconds! once i got to ohsu they admitted me immediately, did a quick ct scan, and i was intubated right before my airway was completely obstructed. from the first zoomcare appointment to my intubation was 6 hours. zoomcare wasted so much time. if they wouldn't have ignored my symptoms i may not have had to be intubated and spent 5 days in the hospital.

so grateful that my dentist recommended carly and orofacial myology! this is not regular speech therapy.... though, it probably should be something all speech therapists are certified in. actually, dare i share, that it should be something all pediatricians, school admins, teachers, speech therapists, dentists, and orthodontists are taught about and should intern in at the very least.
both of my kids looked completely normal from the outside, but had challenges with how their mouth was forming and (as it turns out) facial/jaw/tongue/etc. neuro-muscular control challenges. the visual observation of teeth was only the tip of the iceberg. without going into lots of details, there were speaking, eating, breathing, tongue and lip ties, drooling, tongue thrust, tooth crowding, cross bite, over bite, under bite, and swallowing challenges. we were looking at orthodontists and surgical options by the time my oldest was 6 years old. all i could foresee was debt, time, lots of therapy, and metal mouths for the next 20 years. looking back now, as i write this, i wonder how i thought some braces and time would fix all this.
carly spoke about orofacial myology at a dental conference my pediatric dentist attended. our pediatric dentist had been our dentist for a couple years and had even consulted orthodontists about my kids. after learning from carly, she recommended this therapy for both kids before i got ortho/surgical quotes.
i am so glad she did. carly did an assessment and found some serious challenges. skeptical as i was, she reviewed results of this type of therapy with me and explained that both kids were having neuro-muscular challenges that could be managed to change the shape of their mouth and teeth, breathing, etc. i saw pictures of results and carly made me feel comfortable with her recommendations. after our consult, i came to the conclusion that with this therapy, my kids might not have to have braces or surgery, and that this would help indefinitely for the rest of their lives, so we started therapy that week.
after only 2 weeks of therapy, all signs of sleep apnea were gone and my son hadn't choked on his food at all. (i hadn't put 2:2 together- that breathing challenges and other issues while sleeping were signs of sleep apnea, until it stopped. neither had the pediatrician.) 
carly is so good with kids and personable, using food, straws, mirrors, even toys to get the kids thru the therapy sessions and want to continue practicing at home.
after 4 months carly showed me a side-by-side picture of the mouths of both kids before therapy and after the 4 months. if it wasn't zoomed in from their full face, i don't think i would have said they were from the same people. after 1 year, our pediatric dentist retook xrays and pulled me aside. she told me she needed to talk to carly asap because she'd never seen such natural, results. she said she never would have said (in comparing last year's xrays to this year's), that they were from the same people.
since the 2nd xrays were taken, my older child has lost all but 4 baby teeth. there's now plenty of room for her adult teeth, and they are coming in and straightening out on their own. for both kids, the apnea, ties, crowding, choking, and cross/under bites are gone. we are still working on the speech part, but that'll come in time, the little one's still pretty young.
thank you carly. i appreciate you and wish orofacial myology was something more people in the us understood, recommended, and used in regular practice.

i am writing this review right after leaving, so it is fresh in my mind. 
i have a 15 year old with a bizarre needle phobia.... like off the charts. she had a bleeding disorder as a young child that involved weekly blood draws. the draws just never went well, and as each one happened, my kiddo became more and more damaged. 
don't get me wrong, my daughter is tough. like she will shoulder thump a bigger kid for being a bully. she is not scared of a single thing in the world. she has taken on steep skiing slopes, and handled herself in a raft going down a class five. 
but pop her in a doctor office with a teeny tiny needle, and the girl is a freak-out, sobbing, kicking and screaming mess. it is bad.
over the years, we have gone to places for shots that have held her down, snuck up on her and criticized her to get the shots in her (zoomcare). so of course, all of these tactics have only made things worse. 
today i took her in for 3 vaccines. we have been a bit past due because of the issues. you see, metro peds won't give the shot without consent.
and so for the last 2 years, i have brought my kiddo in numerous times hoping that today would be the day. only with no luck, at all.
today we went in again. she was prepared. she had her numbing cream, she had done her self talk. she felt ready.
and once again, we spent an hour in the office, with no luck. i was so pissed! it was not one of my finer mommy moments.
you see, they told us that today was the last try, if she couldn't do it today then she would have to start exposure therapy with a behavioral health clinic. and as a single mom with three kids, one of which is currently dealing with some severe medical issues that require numerous weekly office visits - my brain just could not wrap around the idea of one more kid in my house requiring weekly doctor visits. 
i lost it. like legit. 
we left the office, and as we went into the hallway towards the elevator, my daughter was profusely apologizing. and, well, i just didn't care. i told her i knew i wasn't handling the moment well.... but come on! then she felt horrible and wanted to go back in, and i said no dice. "they told you that was it! they said no more office visits until you go through therapy!" and she was sobbing begging to go back and make it right. and i was crying.
this lovely lady came out of a side office door, and asked us to come into her office. i was immediately mortified. i glanced in her office door and saw the couch, the teddy bears, the boxes of tissues, along with the inspirational quotes on the wall - and i thought to myself "great, the shrink needs to see me now. awesome" i was absolutely mortified. 
i tried to pass, tell her we were fine, we would just be going home. but she insisted, and explained she was the clinic manger. she wanted to talk and find out how she could help. 
my daughter gladly stormed into her office, so i had no choice. and i was quickly feeling like the worst mom ever. 
the woman (i wish i caught her name), talked us through what was going on, and asked me if i would allow her to give olivia another chance at getting her shots. i figured, what a waste of time, but whatever. she seemed confident, i knew there was no way, but why not really prove to her how crazy the situation is. 
i just could not stop crying; between frustration, exhaustion, embarrassment... i was a mess.
she brought back the same ma that had already spent an hour trying to give my daughter her vaccines. they talked strategy, they came up with a plan. 
so... long story short. it took another hour, but my kiddo got her vaccines! and she walked out proud with her head high. and i walked out still crying but for so many other reasons. 
i am so grateful to this clinic. i have no idea where these ladies get their patience from, but they are saints. 
i really respect their "consent only" policy with shots. and i am so grateful that they did not give up on my girl. 
this is the best in the business, and a very safe place to take your children.

i know she also works with much more complex issues as well, but if you're a young person just starting out on your mental health journey, i would 100% recommend shaudi. she is patient, perceptive, and encouraging. i always leave her office (or our video sessions) feeling empowered. i don't exaggerate when i say she has played a huge role in making me a much more confident woman in every area of my life!

review: im in the clinic room waiting and the staff is really friendly but wait, my 5 year old daughter is about to see a virtual doctor and i think it just sounds hilarious. as long as we get the information and meds we need, i think itll be pretty cool!

i've been a one medical patient for over a year now and never considered leaving a review until now! my pcp patricia evans is amazing and i do love her, but this last month has shown me what one medical is about! 

for the last 4 weeks, i've been in cold/flu season hell, with a sprinkling of other issues to boot. me, who never gets sick and hasn't been to the doctor in nearly a year. smh.

the one medical app is a gamechanger and a time saver. i've received on-call assistance with video chatting for my concerns on several occasions and made appointments with the next available provider at any practice with no long waits for someone to pick up the phone! twice recently, i didn't have the time to wait 3-6 days to see my pcp. the app allowed me to make an appointment with any provider who had room, in one case for same day care! the care was expert, there's never a wait, and my issues have been resolved promptly with care and respect. they have offices at metro center, union station, dupont circle and other areas that are extremely easy to access from the metro anywhere in dc. i've gotten in and out of each appointment in the last month in under 20 minutes, and from where i work, none of the three practices i named are over 15 minutes away! 

lastly, my appointments are always efficient, but the practitioners are never lacking in bedside manner. this practice model is one that all doctors' offices should draw from and, to be honest, i may never go back to traditional medicine. it's worth every penny.

thank you go forward, dr chevon alderson and team! 
i found out about forward on instagram! i was immediately intrigued and wanted to investigate. 
what i found was that the model of this "concierge" type medical group would be a great fit for me. 
i am a middle-aged woman with no pre-existing health conditions, in general good health, rarely see a doctor and am rarely sick. yet there are things i want to keep an eye on and have the support and knowledge of a medical professional. i also have a very full life, i want to know my time is going to be used efficiently. the forward office visits and telehealth option is very appealing to me. 
i have not been disappointed. 
my first visit was extraordinary. 
from the moment i walked in to get checked in i was greeted with efficiency and polite regard. i was impressed with the body scan that gathered baseline info for the doctor. my tech who took blood was great, no pain or poking around for a vein. she offered me snacks knowing i could break my fast once the blood was drawn. 
within minutes dr. chevon alderson arrived, bright and happy to relay all the info that was coming in from the blood. 
super cool technology gave me a detailed view of all my test results. dr. alderson explained everything in terms that were interesting and understandable. 
i gave her my concerns and questions and all the while our conversation was relayed to a medical assistant via microphone to be added to my chart. as we were talking the information was popping up on the screen and would be waiting for me in my forward app. 
i really enjoyed my time with dr alderson and feel confident she will continue to provide me with the care and advice i need going forward!
thank you to all the innovative docs and support who made this possible, it's super cool. 

update: i am receiving covid-19 info and screening questions through my app and have testing available should i feel the need. also have a care giver a text message away if i have any questions or concerns. 
thank you again!

so.....i have the flu, and a compromised immune system due to ms...and i work with the public.  i'm overall very healthy, but thought i should double check because we are currently in the thick of the coronavirus.  i spoke to a doctor on the phone who recommended i go in and get tested.  now, keep in mind, people that are going in to get tested are ill.  they don't feel good.  like myself.  i don't want to go in because i feel terrible, but feel obligated to do so.  there was basically no one there and they got me in after approximately 5 minutes.  so far so good.  after the vitals and a video chat with a doctor, i was to be seen.  in the meantime, they put me in a conference room.  for exactly 45 minutes i waited and listened to the staff chatting, laughing and carrying on through the paper thin walls and then i went home....so here we are in the midst of a global pandemic and this is as streamlined as kaiser can pull off...$900 bucks a month for absolutely nothing ever.  our plan is written in such a way that we will never get any real benefit from it...and we know that's not a mistake...they're sheisters and should be ashamed of themselves...

it's a typical cvs; not usually my first pharmacy choice. but, i was in the area and needed something specific...which they had plenty of.

what i liked best? the self-checkout! one of the four machines was down, but it was nice to be able to get out of there quickly. and, the machines take apple pay. score.

the parking lot is very busy and people zoom around there without really looking around...or caring about running over someone. so, be careful.

i went in for severe depression after my mother passed away. i never actually spoke with a physician and ended up leaving shortly after they took my blood. i am now being charged nearly $2000 for this visit, much of which is for a physician visit, which never happened because i left before a physician talked to me. they were going to get a therapist or someone on a video chat for me but i left before that. i have spoken with the facility and billing department numerous times. they either don't understand what i'm saying or they are simply crooks.
fac_name: Centura Health Urgent Care Canon City

review: these guys are awesome. my doctors have referred me to four other local pt  places over the last five years (i'm a youngster at 74), and vargo easily kicks them all to the curb. vargo is just amazing in their efficiency. while i'm on the table being stretched and strengthened, i look around, and i see what reminds me of a beehive, with all the worker bees zooming around at top speed, all attending to their appointed tasks with 100% efficiency. all under the auspices of erik, who is in charge of what everyone is doing, and treats each patient with caring and respect. the regular staff all are experts at various types of therapy, and even though they do trade off their patients, the results are the same. i'm currently being treated for back pain and weakness related to a fractured vertebrae, and not only are these therapists careful and respectful of every move i make, but so far, every session produces more freedom of movement, and less pain than when i went in. i'm almost ready to put my walker into storage.

chicago family doulas was an essential resource during my first pregnancy. my husband and i wanted to be equipped with as much information and as many tools as possible as new parents, so we utilized several services (a labor doula, prenatal yoga, and classes) offered by chicago family doulas, reviewed below. i can't speak highly enough of our experiences with chicago family doulas!

labor doula cote
after meeting with cote, my husband and i knew we wanted to work with her. her knowledge, energy, and attentive nature were a great match for us right away. she provided us with a very thorough prenatal meeting where we were able to learn more about labor, discuss our birth plan, and practice some prenatal/labor exercises. cote not only made me feel like she respected my goals for the birth, but she also empowered my husband with tools to support me through labor. cote was always available via text or email to check in and ask questions throughout my pregnancy. toward the end of my third trimester, we had a video chat with her to touch base and review our plans for the birth. less than nine hours later, my water broke and my husband and i were on the way to the hospital! during labor, cote coached my husband through giving me massage, counter pressure, and words of encouragement. when he needed a break, she was there to jump in. she also offered recommendations for different labor positions to keep me progressing smoothly. ultimately, i was able the have the beautiful, unmedicated birth i was hoping for thanks to cote's guidance and support; we truly could not have done it without her. after the birth, cote checked in with us via text for several days to see how we were doing and she had a postpartum visit with us once we were home to offer additional advice for healing. she also completed placenta encapsulation for me. overall, cote was amazing to work with and i am so thankful that she was part of my journey in becoming a new mother.

prenatal yoga with liz simbi
liz's prenatal yoga class is great for any expectant mother looking to have a little self-care time while also gently preparing their body for labor. attending these classes allowed me to remain active during my pregnancy in a supportive environment with the guidance of an experienced prenatal yoga teacher and fellow mother. it was definitely something i looked forward to each week during my pregnancy and it helped me feel strong during labor.

yoga for labor with liz simbi
liz's yoga for labor class is great for any mama-to-be and her partner, regardless of prior yoga experience. the class integrates yogic principles, reflection, coping strategies for pain during labor, tips for the birth partner, and partner yoga positions for labor. liz provides great opportunities for couples to discuss their hopes, fears, and plans for labor in an open way and allows participants to practice different positions to have in their toolkit for laboring. i was thankful to connect with my partner during this class and it allowed us to feel prepared to work through birthing our daughter together.

bringing home baby with ashley grosh
the bringing home baby class with ashley was very helpful and made my husband and me feel more prepared to bring home a newborn as new parents. the class covered topics like postpartum recovery for moms, swaddling and diapering, baby carriers and car seat safety, and more. having done a lot of preparation for labor, this class allowed us to learn a bit more about actually caring for a baby. we left with a lot of great information that helped us feel more at ease once our baby arrived. this is definitely a great class for new parents.

i went to see someone here for the first time (emphasis for later). i had called my insurance before to confirm it would be compensated as part of my plan. they confirmed it. zoom billed it inaccurately and i've had to pay out of pocket. they then ignored my several emails to adjust it. i then wasted half a dozen calls with their useless billing department, nichole, who didn't adjust anything. do not come here unless you want to be billed inaccurately and have to follow-up needlessly. go anywhere else.

as a technical consultant, i found the ability to easily send contact information on the website extremely convenient. i also love the ability to select remote services like telehealth. i can personally vouch for the technological proficiency of the counselor emily gilbert. she is highly flexible and able to be reached in a variety of ways and on an array of platforms.

i *love* dr. jensen. i have complex medical issues. while i was undiagnosed i got a lot of negative comments from a lot of doctors suggesting it was all in my head. dr. jensen was a rock through that tough time, always helping as much as he could to alleviate the symptoms that were getting in the way of my life. all throughout the diagnostic process, the extensive reports from all sorts of providers, disability reports, my illnesses becoming more severe over time - he has always been there for me. he is kind. he is thorough. he asks the right questions. he listens. he even offers telemedicine now, which is a lifesaver for me. i have never had any problems with his office. if i have a question, they answer it. if i am having a difficulty with something - like  referral or a prescription refill - they address it. i'm so very happy with him. he checks things other doctors don't, like miconutrient assays (mine showed things that needed to be addressed). he really does his absolute best for you.  he has been my doctor for many years and i'm keeping him.

my mom only checked herself in the er at northeast georgia medical center due to the fact that it's in the country and they aren't as busy. little did she know that it would take 24 hours for her to get a room in the hospital.

yes, she got admitted but 24 hours? are you freaking kidding me? about 5 years ago, my childhood friend first checked herself in at the er here and they didn't help at all. they didn't find anything wrong with her. a few months later, she went to gwinnett medical and they found the cause. she needed a new kidney. since then, she went to emory to get treatment and put her name on the donor list. since then, she moved to mn since they have mayo, the best hospital in the nation!

i went off track but my point is that northest georgia medical center sucks!!!!!!!!!!! 

back to my mom. she has a lot of abdominal pain but they couldn't even come back and tell us anything but we will see. let's wait till the morning.

smh. my daughter is a navy nurse and works in walter reed national military medical center. i video chatted with her so she could talk to her grandma. she wanted to see what is going on.

a few moments later, the nurse came in and just looked at the computer. in the room were also my dad, sister, and brother. my sister asked a lot of questions cause she is worried but the nurse is clueless and gave us uncomfy looks.

she left the room and a guy walked in. he told us that we shouldn't video record the nurse and she feels uncomfy. we're like no one is recording. then i looked at my phone. i said i am video chatting with my daughter. my mom spoke and said that she wanted to speak to her grand daughter.

no apologies!! i said to him, do you want to say hi to my daughter or something? he was taken back. my sister asked him is that why the nurse acted like she couldn't answered questions cause she thought she was on film? he said he could bring her back in. we did not want her to come. she told us she was ready to leave her shift and another nurse will come in! i told him that if she really thought we were recording her, why didn't she say anything???? he said we were too nice and she didn't want to say anything. bull sh!t!! i said, so she is going to get you instead, right? he just answered that he gets called for everything.

poor excuse! no wonder my friend hated this hospital and now i understand. my parents better stop coming to this country hospital and go to the city for better service.

9/2020

my husband and i see dr. conklin here as our pcp and we are very happy with him as our doctor, so much so that i ended up transferring our kids here from their pediatrician. 

dr. conklin takes the time to go through everything with you, and you feel like you have his full attention. he lets you explain what's going on and asks thoughtful questions, and he gives you the time to ask questions of your own. at the pediatricians' office the visits always felt rushed (after you'd first been made to wait ages), the doctor would zoom in and out again within minutes and it was all at such intense speed that most of the time you'd remember the questions you had wanted to ask far too late. 

when needed, i've always been able to make same-day appointments for sick kids, and we've often seen jean cox on those days whom i've also had good experiences with. she's been great with my rambunctious 4-year-old son, who likes her a lot and is amazingly cooperative with her. 

usually the waits are short, and the nurses are very friendly. if there's anything to comment on, it's that the receptionist comes across a bit curt, but that's a minor quibble.

i had quite an unfortunate visit to playa vista medical center. i arrived around 4:30 pm and there were about 4 others in the waiting room. i filled out all the necessary paperwork and then waited to be taken back to an exam room. about 15 minutes had passed before another patient, who walked in 30 seconds before me, inquired how much longer she would have to wait. the nurse at the front desk informed her it would only be another 15-20 minutes. she and i waited over an hour to be placed in an exam room. obviously, this was not pleasant but things happen and i have no control over how much time other patients require.

once i was in the room i was immediately seen by a nurse who took down some basic information regarding my visit. he then left and after 5 minutes or so the doctor came in. she was very short with me and was in the room for about 2-3 minutes. she informed me that she doesn't know what was causing my rash and would prescribe me some antibiotics to help reduce swelling. she then said she was going to fill out the prescription order and someone would be right with me.

this is where my rating went from 3 stars to 1 star. i sat in that exam room for over 30 minutes just staring at the walls waiting for a nurse or doctor to come in, give me more information, and head out considering the doctor already spoke to me. did they forget about me? well, i began growing increasingly impatient and at around the 35-minute mark, opened the door, and walked out of the room. two nurses were standing in the hallway and looked at me like they had just seen a ghost. i said "hey, not sure what's happening but i've been sitting in this room alone waiting for more information. can someone please help me?" a nurse quickly walks over, grabs a clipboard and walks me back into my room. he goes over the medication for about 30 seconds before releasing me and saying i'm good to go home. so yes, they did forget about me. if i did not poke my head out, i can only assume i would've waited in that exam room until they closed. overall not an amazing experience not to mention it was very expensive for a first-time patient. next time i'll just use a virtual doctor service... much easier.

i will not be coming back here and will not be recommending this urgent care to anyone i know.

working with johna has been truly transformative for me. i started working her in early 2019 and i was at the point where traditional therapy and reiki had helped a bit, but didn't really stick for what i needed. i started with a couple in-office session, but due to a move, i've continued working with her fully remote through zoom and phone calls. i was a bit nervous of doing my sessions fully remote, because i usually like to do anything this personal in person, but it honestly hasn't been that different than being in person for me. a lot of this is because johna is great no matter what the medium or communication method; her empathy and intuition is spot on and she is always flexible with how we do our sessions. now onto how she's helped me: on top of the lingering trauma and self-sabotage i couldn't let go of, i was dealing with a serious drop in self-confidence and felt like i didn't have control over my own life. she has helped me pull out of some really painful past trauma that was buried super deep. it's been eye opening to see how much of it shaped my life, my thoughts, and ultimately a lot of the choices i've made. for the first time in my life, i can say i'm actually excited about not knowing what is next for me. i'd be lying if it didn't also cause me moments of intense anxiety, but i'm feeling more confident by the day in the toolset that i've worked on giving myself with johna's help. i can be whole self around her and that makes the sessions extra productive and helpful in helping me reach my life and career goals. thanks johna!
fac_name: Johna Goldenflame, Master EFT, Emotional & Spiritual Counseling

review:
i recently consulted with this endocrine specialist. she was referred by my insurance company as i searched for specialists in this field throughout broward and could not find an appointment within the next few weeks. all of the offices i contacted were booked for 3 - 6 months.

the doctor is board certified in internal medicine, endocrinology diabetes and metabolism. she joined cleveland clinic over a decade ago where she built the inpatient diabetes program, among other important quality-improvement projects. dr. villabona has recently opened up her own practice and i am one of the fortunate ones to be treated by her.

dr. villabona is caring, personable, patient, and thorough. she seemed genuinely interested in getting me back to tip-top health!  i will be returning for a follow up soon, but it's also reassuring to know that i can reach out to her through virtual visits monday thru thursday from 12:30 to 1:00 p.m., as well as early morning on the first saturday of the month. these telemedicine visits are for established patients only, so please call her office for a new patient consult today. her staff is equally knowledgeable in their profession and easy to deal with, which is an added bonus in any practice!

i went on a tuesday right after they opened, barely a wait. i went in with flu-like symptoms (chills,  fever, body aches, sore throat). by the time i was there i was trembling with body aches, sweating, and could hardly move due to the aches and chills. the np was nice enough, not very friendly but she tested me for strep and flu, both which came  back negative. she told me it must be something viral and to take acetaminophen and sent another strep test to the lab, and i had to call back to find out the results after not receiving a call for two days. by thursday, i'm feeling worse. i call a telemedicine doctor who says he thinks i have the flu (nothing to do with minuteclinic but adding some back story). i go back to the minuteclinic to see if they can  give me anything or at least tell me i can go back to work or get me a note.  when i told the latest np, natacha moorer that i was here tuesday she gave a rude look and said "and why are you back again?" and "don't you have a pcp?" (not in dc as i am here as a contract therapist, none of her business honestly). again she says that it's something viral and she doesn't think i'm contagious even though i was having a low grade fever on acetaminophen. i will never go back here again, np moorer was nice to everyone before me but treated me like i was an inconvenience to her. rude practitioners and they rely solely on tests rather than putting together symptoms and listening to the patient.

my husband and i are traveling to thailand, bhutan, bali and singapore and want to get immunizations for that area of the world.  we made an appointment this morning and had such a helpful experience!  angel, the young woman who helped us, was exceptionally warm, welcoming and knowledgeable.  i must admit that i expected to get a 'hard sell' for what immunizations we should get so i did my research online before our appointment.  but to our surprise, there was no hard sell approach.  we had a meeting with a nurse online through zoom, which worked very well.  she gave us a helpful information about immunizations and also other ideas that we will use.  the office visit was $25 compared to other companies charging far more.  we appreciate our experience with wellness mart so much!

i got prk vision correction surgery a little over a month ago. my eyes didn't qualify for lasik because my vision was so bad (at the exam i was measured -9 in both eyes). since prk is a more painful surgery with a slower recovery, i anticipated a lot of pain during and especially after the procedure. i felt no pain during the operation! i started feeling some pain about 2 hours later, probably because the numbing drops wore off, but it wasn't bad. i had 5 types of eyedrops to put in several times a day. for the next few days, i had some discomfort, slight sensitivity to light, and sometimes mild pain. what i didn't expect was the blurriness. i enlarged and bolded the font on my phone, and turned on the zoom function. i stayed home and listened to audiobooks. i was hoping it would be just for a week or so, but it took over 3 weeks to see somewhat clearly. i'm glad i can see clearly now, and it will slowly get clearer in the next few months. my recovery might have been longer due to my very bad eyesight. i was off of work for 1 week and not driving for 2 weeks, but i suggest giving yourself about 3 weeks to do tasks safely and comfortably. i recommend prk with dr. bindi, just keep in mind that it takes a while to get perfect vision.
address: 606 Saratoga Ave  Laser Eye Center of Silicon Valley

review:
needed paperwork for this morning's scheduled 11am appointment in tarpon springs. doctor didn't send it. so i had to wait at the doctor's office after lunch, & then find an open quest that could take me quickly without an appointment. this location  was only 5 miles further, and once i logged in on my mobile phone & pre-registered, the wait was minimal. 

the waiting room was small, with two check in pads. i used one to check in with my qr code. a television kept me entertained until i was called. in addition to health news and weather, it let me know my wait time (3 minutes). antiseptic gel was on a table, if needed. another pad, by the locked door, was available for reaction after the visit ("did you feel well cared for?"). 

once inside (and it was  more than three minutes - 15 minutes until i was called), justine took care of me. her cubicle was neat and tidy. she was thorough & friendly. i was done in 3 min. & i didn't  feel a thing! she was gentle and efficient. i did feel well cared for, & i'd give this place 5 stars if i'd been seen in the advertised time (3, not 15 min.).

action mh 1*

this action urgent care was  terrible.i got there an hour early waiting around. when they finally opened at 9 am you could tell the lady had a chip on her shoulder. it's a also wonderful workers comp case that i've been dealing with for over 2 1/2 years and i've been seen at action urgent care since the beginning. the lady said they didn't have my social security number and i said that they had to because i've been going to action urgent care for 2 1/2 years and they have all my paperwork. ive been to other clinics in safeway stores and the main locations in san jose. i had come for a telehealth/skype style appointment which is pretty much what action urgent care in safeway's or vons is. she said the doctor my appointment is with is off today. i said that was odd because i was physically in the office when he made the appointment specifically for this day and this time. she said i had to reschedule because i had to see this doctor and this doctor only. i said i wasn't gonna come back to this branch and i left. this made me so frustrated because this was two hours wasted time that i could've been at work.
i called action urgent care and ask them about this and they stated that i could see any doctor at any branch and i did not have to specifically see this one doctor.  the lady should have called to see what the doctors were available. i told the customer service line since i was seen at the blossom hill branch. when vladimir was there, service was amazing and last time i was at that branch i was seen two hours after my appointment time and there was only one person in front of me. ridiculous.

i had the absolute worst experience with this dentist. i found the information for getting my teeth whitened on the philips zoom website. i was excited, because the dentist is literally one block from me. i called to book the appointment and had a great first phone call. the lady on the phone suggested that i get my teeth cleaned before the treatment. i was told it would be $90 without the x-ray or $128 with. i booked the appointment, as well as the teeth whitening package. i was so excited. i took a half day off of work in order to make this appointment happen. this morning i received a phone call from their office. apparently they hadn't received my paperwork. the office manager said that my appointment was $228. she was so rude and continuously said, "you got wrong information; that's not my problem". she canceled my appointment and literally hung up the phone when i asked to speak to the dentist. i'm hoping dr. feil sees  this, as i would love to share how this scenario went down. he needs to be  aware that his manager is treating potential customers like they are dirt.
address: 107 W Paces Ferry Rd NW Ste 150

review:
i woke up which i felt was super high blood pressure in somewhat of a panic and needed to see someone right away.  right now with all the caronavirus panic the last thing i wanted was to go into a walk in clinic and wait with a bunch of sick people! (no offence sick people)  super convenient location and when i walked in i was extremely surprised at the decor at the clinic. it's more like a spa feel then a medical clinic.  well not quite a spa, but close! super clean and nicely decorated.   a pleasant gal greeted me at the door and sign me in and i was seen right away by doctor johnson.  

because they are by appointment i was the only one in the clinic which was really nice. the dr never made me feel rushed as a matter of fact i think it's one of the most thorough visits i've had.  she took her time to help me figure out what was going on.

i left with a minor prescription which gave me instant relief.  she also made a couple other recommendations which i super appreciated.  

that was friday, today is saturday and i feel 100% better based on her recommendation.  to top it off she called me today to see how i was doing...really? yes, she did.

i am someone who likes to take care of my own health situation and make sure i understand what's happening typically i'll go see a naturopath and a doctor at the same time to make sure everything's okay and i super appreciated that doctor johnson was open to the naturopathic community as well.  some drs just roll thier eyes.  

i agree with another review in saying this is a brilliant franchise and i'm looking forward to seeing what the new one in bellevue is going to look like the doctor was telling me about how awesome it's going to be.

i would recommend this zoom clinic and dr. johnson to anyone who has an issue.  she's 22 years in practice which is hard to believe because she looks like she's about 35.  

the easy online scheduling is awesome!

i switched my insurance so i never have to come to this office again. 3 hours wait to do a virtual visit with a doctor and who knows how long to see a doctor face to face. i had no choice at the moment but to stay but i definitely never went back after that visit. it's not worth it to me.

fast and reasonable service. i was able to book online for same day service and the doctor had great bedside manners. dr. kendra ho ching addressed my issue quickly and was nice and professional throughout the visit. hands down i recommend zoom.

this is a wholehearted shout-out to pasha marlowe of roots and springs!she is a holistic personal trainer...she is my trainer...and she is a beautiful breath of fresh air in the crowded field of wellness. pasha stands out. she turns the old stories upside down. i never thought i would work with a personal trainer. but pasha is different...and i decided i'm worth the investment to meet my wellness goals as an entrepreneur and mother in my mid-40s!

i came to pasha with some injuries (shoulder issues and si joint dysfunction) and a desire to get stronger and to find relief from chronic stress. i was feeling frustrated because although i live a pretty active life, i have not been able to stick to a strength training routine at home. i don't have time to drive the 30 minutes to the gym (and do not enjoy myself in these settings).

pasha worked with me one-on-one to develop a sensible, fun, and customized program that i could stick to in the comfort of my own home . she is incredibly encouraging, highly intuitive, and wise.

i feel so nurtured and supported in her presence. she has helped me see just how active i already am, and has helped me celebrate in a new way. rather than beating myself up about what i'm not doing, i'm focusing on what i am doing. this mindset shift has allowed me to look forward to my exercises, and i naturally want to keep going and see how strong i can get.

i've had sessions in the studio, but also a zoom video session where i felt like she was right in my home with me! the whole session was recorded too. amazing! so during those times that i can't drive to the studio, i can zoom with pasha and stay on track.

i highly recommend working with pasha. she has also just launched an amazing program: roar with laughter"

i've been to daymark many times over the past several years and over those years i feel like mainly i was treated like a criminal even though i was coming in there voluntarily no court order nothing like that. i would come for group therapy and see a psychologist which typically would take over three months to see one, she didn't really care what i had to say. it was also video conference which seemed crazy to me.  she had no concern for my overall well being and i'm sure i wasn't the first person to feel that way. she did what she needed to do to get me in and out.

after our 95-year-old friend broke her hip and became bedbound, roze room hospice stepped in and took over her care. up to now, the healthcare from her insurer was mediocre at best and we all know how that goes. a parade of beleaguered lvns, nurses and doctors calling it in day in and day out, dealing with yet another patient and never really seeing the person beyond the body in front of them. 

roze room hospice was a breath of fresh air and our saviour. i don't know how we would have taken care of her without the tireless and loving care from them. from the get-go they knew exactly what to do, ordering a hospital bed and all the necessary accouterments for her comfort. they knew the drill--diapers and wipes, her meds, an over the bed table, bedrails, a nebulizer, even an air mattress to keep the bed sores away. within hours of roze room taking over, everything was delivered and put in place, setting the stage for her optimal care and comfort. 

the roze room staff was top notch. laura, joy, keith, dr. patel, eryn, gareth, irma, and libby were all ever so professional and had plenty of heart. like me, they became enamored by our friend and took the time to get to know her.  it showed in how she was treated-- with genuine kindness and heartfelt compassion from day one up until the day of her passing. after her passing, laura and some of the caregivers were kind enough to follow up with condolence texts and touching notes as if she were family.  laura even helped me with returning all of the medical equipment and instructed me on how to safely dispose of the unused medications. 

the one piece of  feedback i would give to roze room is that i wish we had better direct access to her care team via mobile phone and text. i can understand why patients have to go through the main number to get a hold of her caregivers, but direct access to them would have been so much better. that being said, the switchboard was extremely responsive and quick in getting our messages out to the caregivers and laura the rn was kind enough to give me her number so that i could call and text when i needed to. 

thank you roze room. so grateful that you were there for us!

okay, so i never post reviews for anything, but sohomd honestly changed my life not gonna lie. i originally signed up a year or two ago bc they took my insurance (cigna at the time, now aetna), and legally the only way i can get refills on the adhd medication i've been taking for most of my life is to meet with a doctor once a month. i was tired of having to trek to an office in the middle of the workday every month just to confirm my meds were still working, so i signed up for a video appointment with a random doctor here that specialized in adhd. little did i know that would end up totally changing my life.

the guy i got paired up with, dr robert weston, is by far the nicest, kindest, and most caring psychiatrist i have ever worked with. he listens to my needs, cares about my life, and has moved his schedule around to help me in emergencies. after a year of prescription management meetings, he helped me realize i had also been suffering from severe anxiety and depression, and that medication could perhaps help. i was so nervous, but took his suggestion, and it honestly is like i am living in a whole new world. i never knew that life could be so much less exhausting or that i could experience happiness like i do now. i had been living in a fugue state of crippling anxiety and doubt before, but i never would have known it without his help. 

he was so cautious in recommending a medication for me, and made sure to check in regularly after i started taking it to ensure it was going well. 

the one major problem with sohomd is that their administrative system is a hot mess, and there was a 4 month period of time where they suddenly couldn't accept aetna and blue cross due to a weird issue from the insurance companies' end (thankfully fixed as of jan 2020), but robert moved his schedule around to accommodate me anyway so he could make sure i was doing alright, and would call me directly to check in whenever something was going wrong from an admin perspective. 

the level of care i have received from him honestly makes all of the insurance and administrative shenanigans worth it. would highly recommend if you're looking for a caring, flexible psychiatrist, who you can video chat with from a conference room at the office in between work. idk about the other people who work here, but he rocks
